title: Personal Credit Cards: payment crediting, minimum payment due and payment allocation
content:
# Personal Credit Cards: crediting payments, minimum payment due and allocation

This policy covers payments to a Personal Credit Cards account: the day a payment is credited, when a payment made after a non-processing due date is still on time, how the minimum payment due is set, and how a payment is spread across balance types. The percent and floor it refers to are the tier's own minimum payment terms.

## Policy clauses

1. A payment received by 17:00 Eastern Time on a business day is credited that day. One received later, or on a weekend or a Federal Reserve holiday, is credited the next business day.
2. When a payment due date falls on a day the bank does not accept mail or process payments, a payment credited on the next business day is on time.
3. The minimum payment due on a statement is the greater of two figures: the tier's minimum payment floor; and the tier's minimum payment percent of the new statement balance plus the interest and fees billed on that statement, rounded half-up to the cent. It is never more than the statement balance. A statement balance of 0.00 or below has no minimum.
4. Payments are allocated in a fixed order: the part up to the minimum payment goes to the balance type with the lowest APR first; any amount above the minimum goes to the balance type with the highest APR first, then the next highest, as the CARD Act requires.
5. A payment larger than the balance creates a credit balance, which is refunded on request.

## Crediting cases (hypothetical dates)

| Payment received | Credited |
|---|---|
| 16:45 Eastern Time on a Tuesday business day | that Tuesday |
| 17:15 Eastern Time on the same Tuesday | the next business day |
| on a Saturday | the next business day |

A statement whose due date falls on a Sunday, when the bank does not process payments: a payment credited on the Monday business day that follows is on time.

## Minimum payment worked example (hypothetical terms: percent 2%, floor 30.00 USD)

- New statement balance 2000.00 USD, with 20.00 USD interest and no fees billed on it: 2% of 2000.00 is 40.00, plus 20.00 interest, gives 60.00; the greater of 30.00 and 60.00 is 60.00, which is below the statement balance, so the minimum due is 60.00 USD.
- New statement balance 20.00 USD: the greater figure would be the floor of 30.00, but the minimum is never more than the statement balance, so it is 20.00 USD.
- Statement balance of 0.00 or a credit balance: no minimum payment.

## Allocation example (hypothetical balances)

A 250.00 USD payment against a minimum of 50.00 USD, on a card with a balance transfer at 0.00%, purchases at 20.00% and cash advances at 29.00%: the first 50.00 USD goes to the balance transfer balance (lowest APR); the remaining 200.00 USD goes to the cash advance balance first (highest APR), then to purchases.
